findings.title: Remove the old local recovery credential when updating user storage
findings.body: A user can already have locally stored recovery codes, particularly because registration previously always created them locally. If the user-storage provider accepts the new set, this path leaves that existing local credential untouched. Keycloak's credential validation can still validate the old local codes when external validation fails, so regenerating recovery codes does not revoke the previous set. Remove the local recovery credential after a successful external update and test regeneration for a user with existing local codes.

findings.title: Remove exhausted recovery credentials from their owning storage
findings.body: The new lookup can return a credential owned by user storage, but the subsequent exhaustion branch still calls removeStoredCredentialById, which deletes credentials from Keycloak's credential store rather than the external provider. An external provider retaining an exhausted credential therefore remains configured. If the user abandons login before completing regeneration, the next login can select that exhausted credential and fail in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean when getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() encounters an empty Optional. Disable or remove the exhausted external credential through the user-storage SPI.

findings.title: Make the test provider consume recovery codes
findings.body: The new validator only checks membership in the original code list; it never persists consumption or advances the next-code state. getCredentials also reconstructs a completely unused model from that same list on every call. Consequently, this fixture accepts the same recovery code indefinitely, always requests code zero, and never reaches exhaustion. The added single-login test passes without exercising the essential single-use contract or exhausted-credential handling. Persist and expose used-code state, and test subsequent logins, replay rejection, and exhaustion.
